results.notes: Treatment: Human-AI condition (editor); control: Human condition. Study 1: CreativeCollabAI_Study1.sav, condition_coded 1 = Human, 2 = Human-AI editor, 3 = AI-only benchmark; outcome = Expert_creativity. Mapping follows the paper's condition ordering and reproduces Table 1 (PDF p. 4) and counts (PDF pp. 2, 4). The file contains 146 rows: 48 human, 48 editor and 50 AI-only poems. Exclude condition 3 from the participant contrast. Retain all 96 human rows, whose AC entries are study or Study; the single missing user_time value is unrelated to this outcome. The deposit already contains the reported analyzed sample; there are no additional attention-check exclusions to apply. The inconsistent printed recruitment arithmetic (101 recruited, six excluded, 96 analyzed) and omnibus error df of 145 cannot be resolved from the posted participant sample. The exact human mean is 18.225, which rounds half-up to the printed 18.23. Reproduction criteria are the extracted table arm means and sample SDs (two decimal places, decimal half-up rounding) and printed participant counts (exact). All must match before the contrast is estimated. The full 11-page markdown, including Methods, references and end matter, was read; it contains no appendix. Cited PDF text and Tables 1 and 2 were checked with pymupdf, including find_tables(). The two-page deposited syntax was read as text only and identifies the expert outcome variables. Each human row represents one participant's sole poem. The SAV files provide one expert-creativity score per poem, without individual-rater scores or participant IDs; the underlying aggregation over raters cannot be independently reconstructed. The supplied score is the participant-level outcome, and there are no repeated outputs to average. SDs use n - 1. Difference is the treatment mean minus the control mean in the original 1-40 creativity-score units. Individual randomization is reported on PDF p. 9. OLS uses only the two contrasted arms, with an intercept and treatment indicator; HC2 standard errors are verified against sqrt(s_t^2/n_t + s_c^2/n_c). The paper's original LSD p-values use a three-condition ANOVA error term and are not the reproduction target or the source of the new standard error. Both studies are between-person designs, so round is all and no first_round or paired result applies. No diversity outcome occurs in the extraction.

Treatment: Human-AI condition (editor); control: Human condition. Study 2: CreativeCollabAI_Study2.sav, string condition 1 = Human, 2 = Human-AI editor, 3 = Co-creator human-AI; outcome = expert_creativity. Mapping is independently corroborated by dummy_1 and dummy_2 and the paper's explicit dummy definitions (PDF p. 7). All 152 rows are retained (51 human, 50 editor, 51 co-creator), matching counts on PDF pp. 4-5. No attention-check exclusions were reported; study, Study and the quoted 'study' response are retained. Each contrast selects only its named two arms. Arm summaries reproduce Table 2 (PDF p. 7). The data support the expert human SD of 4.98 in that table; the conflicting prose value 9.24 (PDF p. 6) belongs to self-reported creativity. The paper also prints both 0.278 and 0.280 around the co-creator/human comparison; neither is used to derive the requested HC2 SE. The three Study 2 results share participants and are not independent estimates.
